title: Answer 404 instead of 403 for posts you don't own

review.why: The PR intentionally changes the HTTP status code from 403 to 404 when users attempt to edit or delete posts they don't own, as documented in the PR description. Tests are updated to match the new expected behavior, confirming this is an announced change, not a regression.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Editing or deleting someone else's post now answers 404 Not Found instead of 403 Forbidden, so the API doesn't confirm which post ids exist.". The diff changes abort(403) to abort(404) in both edit and delete endpoints when the post author doesn't match the current user, exactly as described.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Editing or deleting someone else's post now answers 404 Not Found instead of 403 Forbidden, so the API doesn't confirm which post ids exist.". The diff changes abort(403) to abort(404) in both edit and delete endpoints when the post author doesn't match the current user, exactly as described.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR intentionally changes unauthorized edit/delete responses from 403 Forbidden to 404 Not Found to avoid leaking post existence.

suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as user A, create a post, then authenticate as user B and PUT /api/posts/<post_id> with JSON {'text': 'x'}; read response status (404) and JSON body code/message/description.
suspicions.evidence: Probe round2 probe_s1_unauthorized_edit sent PUT /api/posts/151; base returned 403 with description 'You don't have the permission to access the requested resource...' and head returned 404 with description 'The requested URL was not found on the server...'.

suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as user A, create a post, then authenticate as user B and DELETE /api/posts/<post_id>; read response status (404) and JSON body code/message/description.
